fit: OddsJam is a scanner: it surfaces arbitrage, +EV, middles and low holds across many books and refreshes live bets on its own, so it suits someone who wants a long list of plays to work through. Unabated is built around one fair line of its own making, with props tools on its cheapest plan, so it suits someone who wants a single sharp price to bet against rather than a feed of alerts. If you mostly bet player props, the Unabated props plan is the narrower and cheaper fit; if you want every opportunity type in one place, OddsJam covers more of them.

Both are arbitrage scanners, and the difference is reach against price. BetBurger covers far more bookmakers and adds value bets and middles, but it prices in euros per thirty days and charges the most for live. RebelBetting covers fewer bookmakers, shows a US visitor dollar prices, and offers a free trial, which lets you check its arbs against your own books before paying. If you bet at a handful of US books, more reach mostly means arbs you cannot place.

Betstamp PRO is a professional odds screen: its base plan covers pre-game moneylines, spreads and totals, with paid add-ons and props and live quoted by its sales team. OddsJam bundles the screen with recommendations, putting arbitrage, +EV, middles, low holds and a promo converter in one plan billed by the day. Betstamp PRO suits a bettor who wants the prices and makes their own calls; OddsJam suits one who wants the tool to propose the bets.
